newsitem.title: PORTUGAL: Portugal sought yen funds because cheaper - IGCP.
newsitem.headline: Portugal sought yen funds because cheaper - IGCP.

text.p: Portugal's 10 billion yen dual-currency bond, announced on Wednesday, will have an all-in-cost of six-month Lisbor less 30 basis points which is cheaper than raising funds on the domestic market, the president of the Institute for Public Credit Management (IGCP) said.
Vitor Bento said that the yen operation, like some recent commercial paper operations, yielded funds at lower rates than could be achieved by selling Treasury bills.
The IGCP rejected all bids at its offer to sell 15 billion escudos of three-month bills on Wednesday.
The dual-currency, two-year bond carries a coupon of five percent.
